summary.intent: Implement SDK-driven E2E and load test suites as two new workspace packages (tests/sdk-e2e and tests/load) to replace flaky Playwright browser automation with direct CipherBoxClient calls, then run them against a local stack and get PR #318 merged.
summary.outcome: Both packages were created and all 83 SDK E2E tests pass locally. A throttle bypass mechanism (BypassableThrottlerGuard + X-Throttle-Bypass header) was implemented to allow tests to run against production-throttled staging. Load tests run successfully with useful baseline metrics. PR #318 went through multiple rounds of automated review comments, all resolved.

repo: The orval-generated API client functions (e.g. ipnsControllerPublishRecord) use a module-level singleton config via setApiClientConfig in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts — all sdk-core functions that call generated API functions depend on this singleton being set correctly before each call

ThrottlerGuard is applied per-controller via @UseGuards, not globally — 7 controllers plus 11 individual endpoints with @Throttle() decorators; IPNS publish endpoint has a strict 10 publishes/min limit
test-login endpoint has its own strict throttle (5 per 15 min) separate from the general controller throttle
NODE_ENV in apps/api/.env takes precedence over the shell env var when running nest start --watch, so setting NODE_ENV=test in the shell doesn't override a .env file with NODE_ENV=development
pnpm install from workspace root updates the lockfile correctly for new packages added to tests/*; the workspace.yaml already covers tests/*

API unit test specs use .overrideGuard(ThrottlerGuard) targeting the @nestjs/throttler class — when swapping to a custom guard subclass, all specs must be updated to override the new guard class or NestJS DI resolution fails
crypto.getRandomValues() has a 65,536 byte limit per call — generating random Uint8Arrays larger than 64KB requires chunked generation
The CipherBoxClient exposes getFolderTree() as a public method, making (client as any).folderTree casts unnecessary
setApiClientConfig accepts a defaultHeaders option (added in this session) which propagates to all axios requests via the cached axios instance

code.finding: Module-level singleton _config and _axiosInstance; getCachedInstance() returns a shared axios instance keyed by baseUrl — adding defaultHeaders required invalidating the cache when headers change

New BypassableThrottlerGuard extends ThrottlerGuard; uses Buffer.from + crypto.timingSafeEqual for constant-time comparison; guards against non-ASCII secrets via byteLength check; skips bypass in NODE_ENV=production
Gold standard test-harness pattern: test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → POST /vault/init → setApiClientConfig → new CipherBoxClient → registerFolder
createTestContext() and createTestAccount() extracted from integration.test.ts pattern; testFetch() wraps global fetch with Authorization + X-Throttle-Bypass headers for raw HTTP calls in test suites
switchTo() must call setApiClientConfig for each account before sdk-core IPNS operations; must also update defaultHeaders to preserve bypass header across account switches

createClientPool creates N accounts in parallel batches reusing createTestAccount from test-harness; setApiClientConfig is called once with shared baseUrl and first client's token — works because all clients share baseUrl and tokens are per-request via closure

workflow: Running nest start --watch (dev mode) handles .env loading correctly; running node dist/main.js directly does not load .env — always use pnpm --filter api dev for test runs against the compiled API
When a pre-commit hook runs markdownlint, inline code in markdown files needs blank lines before/after fenced code blocks and no bare URLs without angle brackets
1Password SSH agent for commit signing is not available to background Bash tool processes — commits from background tasks may time out waiting for the agent; foreground commits work fine
CodeRabbit generates review comments referencing vitest CLI flags incorrectly (e.g. confusing Jest --testPathPattern with vitest equivalents) — these are safe to dismiss as not applicable

Resolving GitHub PR review threads requires two steps: REST API reply (in_reply_to with integer comment ID) then GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation (with string thread node ID); the two IDs are different

friction: The module-level singleton in setApiClientConfig forced a switchTo() hack in multi-account test fixtures and required adding defaultHeaders to propagate the bypass header — this is a known design gap tracked as a todo

crypto.getRandomValues() silently fails for arrays >65536 bytes; the error was swallowed by Promise.allSettled in the load test harness, making it very hard to diagnose — appeared as '0 ops, 3 clients failed'
Multiple rounds of sed-based bulk edits to test files got corrupted (mismatched parentheses from fetchHeaders wrapping) — required rewriting files from scratch
The 1Password SSH agent timed out for background bash commands during commit signing, requiring retries and user intervention

NestJS DI fails with a cryptic 'THROTTLER:MODULE_OPTIONS' error when test specs override ThrottlerGuard but controllers import BypassableThrottlerGuard — the error message doesn't indicate a guard class mismatch

Per-endpoint @Throttle() decorators on IPNS publish (10/min) still caused 429s during load tests even after adding the bypass guard — the bypass guard covers controller-level throttling but the per-endpoint decorator behavior needed separate investigation
open_items: Refactor api-client from module-level singleton to instance-scoped axios: configure orval to generate functions accepting an axios instance parameter, thread it through sdk-core SdkContext, have CipherBoxClient own its instance — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md

Investigate throttle bypass gap for per-endpoint @Throttle decorators: verify X-Throttle-Bypass header reaches IPNS publish endpoint, determine if 429s come from API throttler or upstream IPFS, extend bypass to cover all 11 @Throttle-decorated endpoints — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-investigate-throttle-bypass-gap-for-per-endpoint-throttle-decorators.md
Load test scenarios fail silently — all clients rejected shows as '0 ops' with no error output; need better error surfacing when the entire workload crashes before any metrics are recorded

Raw fetch() calls in vault-lifecycle, share-operations, and invite-link test suites should migrate to the generated API client functions once the singleton refactor lands — currently wrapped in testFetch() as an intermediate workaround

Load tests measure single-node throughput on staging but cannot test horizontal scaling effectiveness — a separate load test strategy targeting the production cluster with real throttle limits and distributed source IPs is needed for cluster validation
The TESTING_STRATEGY.md document in tests/ captures the tiered throttle bypass decision and scaling implications — should be kept updated as the architecture evolves
